News Summary; Open Models; Built for Sovereign Enterprise-Scale Deployment
Exhibit 99.1 opening partnership and integration paragraphs

pue.boundary: Palantir is a software supplier; associated hosted or customer infrastructure is a separate deployment perimeter
pue.basis: No supplier PUE meaningfully measures software sold. Matched customer-site PUE and even defensible proxy inputs are unavailable; no universal default or generation/IT ratio used.

model.revenue_scope: attributable incremental AI software revenue only; total company revenue is a contextual control, not a model numerator
model.capacity_time_basis: sum(active_customer_AI_IT_MW * active_days_in_period) / period_days; apply matching cohort physical utilization only to the separately labeled effective-MW extension

formulas.conditional_same_spend_volume_break_even: d/(1-d), only for comparable unit price decline d with unchanged eligible basket; no Palantir realized d disclosed

assumptions.basis: Run-rate convention only, not a revenue forecast. Not applied to total-company revenue as AI numerator.
No deployment cohort or energy data supports numeric low/base/high cases.

sensitivity.basis: For the same matched facility footprint, attributable revenue per effective IT MW is R_annual * PUE/(facility_MW * utilization). For disclosed IT MW, omit PUE. No numeric range without company inputs.
sensitivity.cost_implication: An unrelieved dollar spend floor can limit savings from falling unit prices; exact credits, repricing, service substitution and obligations are not disclosed.

model.replacement_implications: No disclosed Palantir-owned GPU fleet or residual-value guarantee maps to these contracts. Provider hardware replacement can still affect prices, service quality or required spend; contract technology-refresh rights are missing.

structured_deals.economic_effect: At least $5.6B over ten contract years to 2036-02-29; annual minima $268M-$979M. Prior payment obligations of that amended contract terminated. Supplier-price declines do not automatically lower a dollar minimum; rate-reset and eligible-service terms remain unknown.

Compute/inference endpoints intended inside Palantir enterprise perimeter; modular deployment at already powered sites discussed. No disclosed quantified offtake, pricing, take-or-pay, financing guarantee, revenue split or firm delivery date. Do not attribute March minimum-spend contract to Nebius.

Nemotron customization with Foundry/AIP can support open-model software monetization. No matched workload benchmark, MW, GPU count, contract value or measured savings; do not book forecast benefit as revenue.
$500M capacity, zero drawn, March 31 2027 maturity, $50M minimum-liquidity covenant. No compute-project debt allocation disclosed.

Primarily corporate office leases: $292.539M undiscounted gross commitments at December 31 2025, $229.338M discounted liability; no GPU-MW inference. June ROU asset $230.268M is not installed compute capacity.

$452.612M current/noncurrent customer deposits are cancelable-contract balances; pro-rata refund terms mean they cannot be treated as irrevocable GPU-purchase financing. RPO $4.9B is separately defined.
Defined strategic commercial contract subset supplied about $3M H1 revenue. Noncash consideration/investment risk remains disclosed; do not generalize that subset to all reciprocal business.

findings: Confirmed: a ten-year $5.6B cloud minimum-spend agreement shows material contracted infrastructure exposure despite low owned capex; the counterparty is unnamed.
Confirmed: Q2 cloud cost in cost of revenue rose $89M year on year, and R&D cloud cost rose $25M. These are cost increases, not total spending or hardware volumes.

Strongest disconfirming evidence to immediate financing stress: Q2 operating cash flow $1.216B, approximately $9.225B cash/equivalents/Treasuries and zero outstanding debt at June 30. Reported gross margin increased to 85%.
Derived: Q2 cash capex was 0.752% of total revenue; operating cash flow less cash capex was $1.202B. Neither measure removes cloud minimum commitments.
Company claim: sovereign open-model architecture is a monetization route for Palantir and a distribution route for Nebius; financial benefit and delivered MW are not quantified.

Inference: software revenue can benefit from useful model improvements without proportional increases in GPU count. The available data cannot establish token-volume elasticity, revenue per effective MW or price-versus-quantity decomposition.
No inherited quantitative Palantir estimate was promoted to verified; the prior entity method was a queued research stub.
gaps: Incremental AI/AIP-only recognized software revenue, allocation between Palantir-hosted and customer-hosted workloads, and separately identified pass-through compute/hardware are not disclosed.
Matching-period active customer IT MW, GPU/model counts, activation dates, physical utilization and energy allocation are not disclosed; no period-average capacity can be reconstructed.
Customer-site total and IT energy, measured operational PUE, and matched technology/geography proxy inputs are not disclosed. Software supplier PUE is not_applicable.

Full March cloud amendment, provider identity, eligible-service definitions, annual schedule, rate resets, credits, shortfall relief, unused-spend carryforward, paid-to-date and remaining minimum commitments are not public in reviewed documents.

Nebius agreement economics, revenue share, committed MW, GPU ownership, acceptance terms, integration completion date, PPA/SPV/guarantee details and financing obligations are not stated in the reviewed announcement.

No selected-company compute-project PPA, financing SPV/VIE, GPU/facility lease or residual-value guarantee identified in reviewed filing notes and exhibit indexes. This is bounded negative evidence, not proof none exists.

No realized token price/volume, task-level useful throughput, matched open-versus-proprietary unit costs or deployment revenue reported; no empirical Jevons conclusion or chips/MW estimate is supportable.

Official CEO letter URL returned only a page shell; official earnings webcast was located but a readable primary transcript was not retrieved. The complete issuer presentation, earnings exhibit and filings supply the financial evidence.
